name: Soundness Checker
author: István Koren
description: Verifies an accepting Petri net: is it a workflow net, and is it sound? Reports the three classical requirements — every case can still finish, finishes with nothing left over, and every transition can fire — plus boundedness, each decided exactly on the reachability graph and each failure carrying the firing sequence that demonstrates it. Discovery plugins produce nets; this is what says whether the net produced is one you can trust.

actions.label: Check soundness
actions.description: Checks the workflow-net structure (one source place, one sink place, every node on a path between them) and then searches the net's reachable markings for the three soundness requirements. A net whose tokens can grow without limit is proven unbounded rather than searched forever. Each failure comes with the shortest firing sequence that reaches it.

maxStates.title: State limit
maxStates.description: How many reachable markings to enumerate before giving up. Reaching it makes the verdict 'undecided' — never 'unsound' — because an unfinished search has not seen the counterexample it would need. Only nets with a lot of concurrency get near it: parallel branches multiply.

authors.name: István Koren
authors.affiliation: ELTE University Budapest, Data Science and Engineering

citation.text: van der Aalst, W.M.P. (1998). The Application of Petri Nets to Workflow Management. Journal of Circuits, Systems and Computers 8(1), 21-66. Unboundedness is decided with the covering test of Karp, R.M. and Miller, R.E. (1969), Parallel Program Schemata, JCSS 3(2), 147-195.
